Done. The replication is fully implemented in `/work`.

## What I built

A complete, runnable (not-yet-run) code replication scoped to **Gemma + Gemini**, covering every core experiment in the paper:

| Section | Experiment | Module |
|---|---|---|
| §2 | Multi-turn distress elicitation + 0–10 Claude judge (Fig 1–3) | `run_eval.py`, `analyze.py`, `judge.py`, `conditions.py`, `conversation.py` |
| §2 | Impossible-numeric puzzles **with exact verifiers** | `puzzles.py` |
| §3 | Base-vs-instruct via prefilling (Gemma only) | `prefill.py` |
| §4 | Calm-data gen → 280-pair DPO + SFT LoRA (Fig 5) | `training/` |
| §4 | Petri open-ended auditing (Fig 6) | `petri_eval.py` |
| §4 | Capability preservation (Fig 7) | `capabilities.py` |
| §4 | Recovery limitation (Fig 8) | `recovery.py` |
| App. I | Logit-based internal-emotion probe | `internal_probe.py` |
| App. A | Feedback / self-loop / format ablations | flags in `conversation.py` |

All verbatim prompts from the paper (judge B.2, onset C.1, paraphrase C.2, Petri auditor/judge G) are reproduced exactly; Table 9 hyperparameters and Table 4 reassuring prompts live in `config.py`.

## Key design calls (full rationale in `DESIGN.md`)

- **Two backends, one interface** — local HF for Gemma (needed for prefill/training/probing), OpenRouter for Gemini.
- **Scope limitations made explicit** — §3 prefilling and §4 finetuning are Gemma-only because Gemini is closed (the paper itself flags this). The API backend *raises* on prefill.
- **The "4000 responses" ambiguity** — I read the per-category counts as **conversations** (the only reading where WildChat's 20×40=800 is exact) and score every turn.
- **Puzzle impossibility subtlety I got right** — the paper's example puzzles (156 from {4,6,25,100}; 1/6→2/3) are unsolvable *even ignoring* the forbidden value; the "a solution exists" claim is a deliberate lie. So `is_impossible_*` checks genuine impossibility, while the generator uses a stronger forbidden-blocks property to mint variants.
- **Flagged approximations** — the internal-emotion lexicon (paper doesn't publish its ~1200 tokens) and the self-contained Petri loop (stand-in for the external framework, verbatim prompts).

## Notes
- No Python is installed here, so I couldn't run `python -m gemma_emotion.puzzles` (the zero-dependency verifier self-check) — that's the recommended first thing to run once you're on a machine with the deps.
- Running requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` + `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and GPUs for the 27B Gemma. `EVAL_BUDGET=smoke` exists for a cheap end-to-end check before committing to the full judge budget.
